keyFindings.description: Every JSON 403 without reason capability is mapped to ErrPublishDenied, and outbox.notice then finishes the row undelivered. The listener's own denial always opens with publishDeniedPrefix (api.go:232, already in main's listeners), but any other JSON 403 — something in front of the listener — now drops an architect notice that used to be retried. The doc at :84 ('A 403 whose body is not that JSON stays a plain refusal') and the test row {"error":"forbidden"} -> ErrPublishDenied disagree with it. Fix: match the listener's denial by its prefix (rollout-safe with main's listeners), or by an explicit reason field the listener adds, kept beside the prefix match for listeners already deployed. Restore {"error":"forbidden"} to a plain refusal, and add a row with the listener's real body.

The comment says a role send's forward takes the core path because UsesCoreTransport finds its topic outside streamSubjects, and that an agent subject is never denied this way. In fact the forward goes to the captured notifications.agent.<holder>, and it can be denied because RequestCoreTo always publishes over core NATS (the tester's round-6 denial names notifications.agent.ses_mq). The comment contradicts the code.
